title: [.Net] Memory management problem with short-lived godot collections
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducable in v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]
- Reproducable in v4.5
- Reproducable in v4.6-dev6

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Single-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8142) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700H (20 threads) - 15.73 GiB memory

### Issue description

Memory Leaks when calling `GetUsedCells()` in a `TileMapLayer` with C# script.  

In my case I'm calling `GetUsedCells()` from a `_PhysicsProcess()` in a C# Tool Script as I want to monitor cell changes (suspeciously `change` signal not working in editor), and the memory leak is observable through the Windows Task Manager when `TileMapLayer` contains a large sum of cells.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92b6904c-4045-4610-befa-01f67546f869)

This bug can be reproduced in v4.5, v4.5.1 and v4.6-dev6.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new Godot project in v4.5.1.mono.stable
2. Create a 2D Scene with a `TileMapLayer` node
3. Add cells to the `TileMapLayer`. The more cells added, the more significant the leak is.
4. Attach a C# script that calls `GetUsedCells()` frequently, e.g. from `_Process` or `_PhysicsProcess`

```CSharp
using Godot;

public partial class Leak : TileMapLayer
{
    public override void _PhysicsProcess(double delta)
    {
        base._PhysicsProcess(delta);
        GetUsedCells();
    }
}
```

5. Run the scene, and monitor the memory usage of the process

> Note that it also occurs in Editor in a `[Tool]` script

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This bug is C#-specific.

[tilemaplayer-memory-leak.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24022882/tilemaplayer-memory-leak.zip)
